   106→                    ),
   107→                },
   108→                "sort": {
   109→                    "type": "string",
   110→                    "enum": ["most_downloaded", "highest_rated", "newest"],
   111→                    "description": "Sort order. Default: 'most_downloaded'.",
   112→                },
   113→                "period": {
   114→                    "type": "string",
   115→                    "enum": ["day", "week", "month", "year", "all_time"],
   116→                    "description": "Time period for sorting. Default: 'all_time'.",
   117→                },
   118→                "nsfw": {
   119→                    "type": "boolean",
   120→                    "description": "Include NSFW results. Default: false.",
   121→                },
   122→                "max_results": {
   123→                    "type": "integer",
   124→                    "description": "Max results (1-20). Default: 10.",
   125→                },
   126→            },
   127→            "required": ["query"],
   128→        },
   129→    },
   130→    {
   131→        "name": "get_civitai_model",
   132→        "description": (
   133→            "Get detailed info for a specific CivitAI model by ID. Returns "
   134→            "all versions, files, example images, description, and stats. "
   135→            "Use after search_civitai to get full details before recommending."
   136→        ),
   137→        "input_schema": {
   138→            "type": "object",
   139→            "properties": {
   140→                "model_id": {
   141→                    "type": "integer",
   142→                    "description": "CivitAI model ID (from search results).",
   143→                },
   144→            },
   145→            "required": ["model_id"],
   146→        },
   147→    },
   148→    {
   149→        "name": "get_trending_models",
   150→        "description": (
   151→            "Get trending models on CivitAI this week. Quick way to discover "
   152→            "what's popular right now. Useful for proactive recommendations: "
   153→            "'A new LoRA is trending and compatible with your workflow.'"
   154→        ),
   155→        "input_schema": {
   156→            "type": "object",
   157→            "properties": {
   158→                "model_type": {
   159→                    "type": "string",
   160→                    "enum": ["checkpoint", "lora", "controlnet", "embedding", "vae", "upscaler"],
   161→                    "description": "Filter by type. Default: all types.",
   162→                },
   163→                "base_model": {
   164→                    "type": "string",
   165→                    "description": (
   166→                        "Filter by base: 'sd15', 'sdxl', 'flux', 'sd3', 'pony'."
   167→                    ),
   168→                },
   169→                "period": {
   170→                    "type": "string",
   171→                    "enum": ["day", "week", "month"],
   172→                    "description": "Trending period. Default: 'week'.",
   173→                },
   174→                "max_results": {
   175→                    "type": "integer",
   176→                    "description": "Max results (1-20). Default: 10.",
   177→                },
   178→            },
   179→            "required": [],
   180→        },
   181→    },
   182→]
   183→
   184→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   185→# Helpers
   186→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   187→
   188→def _strip_html(text: str) -> str:
   189→    """Remove HTML tags from CivitAI descriptions."""
   190→    if not text:
   191→        return ""
   192→    return re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", text).strip()
   193→
   194→
   195→def _build_headers() -> dict:
   196→    """Build request headers with optional auth."""
   197→    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
   198→    if CIVITAI_API_KEY:
   199→        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {CIVITAI_API_KEY}"
   200→    return headers
   201→
   202→
   203→def _check_installed(model_type: str, files: list[dict]) -> bool:
   204→    """Check if any file from a CivitAI model version is installed locally."""
   205→    if not MODELS_DIR.exists():
   206→        return False
   207→    subdir = _TYPE_TO_SUBDIR.get(model_type, "")
   208→    if subdir:
   209→        target_dir = MODELS_DIR / subdir
   210→        if target_dir.exists():
   211→            for f in files:
   212→                name = f.get("name", "")
   213→                if name and (target_dir / name).exists():
   214→                    return True
   215→    # Fallback: search all model subdirectories
   216→    for d in sorted(MODELS_DIR.iterdir()):
   217→        if d.is_dir():
   218→            for f in files:
   219→                name = f.get("name", "")
   220→                if name and (d / name).exists():
   221→                    return True
   222→    return False
   223→
   224→
   225→def _parse_model(model: dict) -> dict:
   226→    """Extract key fields from a CivitAI model response."""
   227→    stats = model.get("stats", {})
   228→    creator = model.get("creator", {})
   229→    versions = model.get("modelVersions", [])
   230→    model_type = model.get("type", "")
   231→
   232→    latest = versions[0] if versions else {}
   233→    latest_files = latest.get("files", [])
   234→
   235→    return {
   236→        "id": model.get("id"),
   237→        "name": model.get("name", ""),
   238→        "type": model_type,
   239→        "creator": creator.get("username", ""),
   240→        "rating": round(stats.get("rating", 0), 2),
   241→        "downloads": stats.get("downloadCount", 0),
   242→        "favorites": stats.get("favoriteCount", 0),
   243→        "tags": sorted(model.get("tags", []))[:8],
   244→        "base_model": latest.get("baseModel", ""),
   245→        "latest_version": latest.get("name", ""),
   246→        "nsfw": model.get("nsfw", False),
   247→        "url": f"https://civitai.com/models/{model.get('id', '')}",
   248→        "installed": _check_installed(model_type, latest_files),
   249→    }
   250→
   251→
   252→def _parse_model_detail(model: dict) -> dict:
   253→    """Parse full model detail including versions and files."""
   254→    stats = model.get("stats", {})
   255→    creator = model.get("creator", {})
   256→    model_type = model.get("type", "")
   257→
   258→    versions = []
   259→    for v in model.get("modelVersions", [])[:5]:
   260→        files = []
   261→        for f in v.get("files", []):
   262→            files.append({
   263→                "name": f.get("name", ""),
   264→                "size_kb": round(f.get("sizeKB", 0)),
   265→                "format": f.get("metadata", {}).get("format", ""),
   266→            })
   267→        images = [
   268→            img.get("url", "")
   269→            for img in v.get("images", [])[:3]
   270→            if img.get("url")
   271→        ]
   272→        versions.append({
   273→            "id": v.get("id"),
   274→            "name": v.get("name", ""),
   275→            "base_model": v.get("baseModel", ""),
   276→            "created_at": v.get("createdAt", "")[:10],
   277→            "download_url": v.get("downloadUrl", ""),
   278→            "files": files,
   279→            "example_images": images,
   280→            "installed": _check_installed(model_type, v.get("files", [])),
   281→        })
   282→
   283→    return {
   284→        "id": model.get("id"),
   285→        "name": model.get("name", ""),
   286→        "type": model_type,
   287→        "creator": creator.get("username", ""),
   288→        "description": _strip_html(model.get("description", ""))[:500],
   289→        "tags": sorted(model.get("tags", []))[:10],
   290→        "nsfw": model.get("nsfw", False),
   291→        "stats": {
   292→            "downloads": stats.get("downloadCount", 0),
   293→            "favorites": stats.get("favoriteCount", 0),
   294→            "rating": round(stats.get("rating", 0), 2),
   295→            "rating_count": stats.get("ratingCount", 0),
   296→        },
   297→        "versions": versions,
   298→        "url": f"https://civitai.com/models/{model.get('id', '')}",
   299→    }
   300→
   301→
   302→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   303→# Handlers
   304→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   305→
   306→def _handle_search_civitai(tool_input: dict) -> str:
   307→    query = tool_input["query"]
   308→    model_type = tool_input.get("model_type")
   309→    base_model = tool_input.get("base_model")
   310→    sort = tool_input.get("sort", "most_downloaded")
   311→    period = tool_input.get("period", "all_time")
   312→    nsfw = tool_input.get("nsfw", False)
   313→    max_results = min(tool_input.get("max_results", 10), 20)
   314→
   315→    params: dict = {
   316→        "query": query,
   317→        "limit": max_results,
   318→        "sort": _SORT_MAP.get(sort, "Most Downloaded"),
   319→        "period": _PERIOD_MAP.get(period, "AllTime"),
   320→        "nsfw": str(nsfw).lower(),
   321→    }
   322→
   323→    if model_type:
   324→        civitai_type = _TYPE_MAP.get(model_type.lower())
   325→        if civitai_type:
   326→            params["types"] = civitai_type
   327→
   328→    if base_model:
   329→        bm = _BASE_MODEL_MAP.get(base_model.lower(), base_model)
   330→        params["baseModels"] = bm
   331→
   332→    if not CIVITAI_LIMITER().acquire(timeout=5.0):
   333→        return to_json({"error": "Rate limited — too many CivitAI requests. Try again shortly."})
   334→
   335→    try:
   336→        with httpx.Client() as client:
   337→            resp = client.get(
   338→                f"{CIVITAI_API}/models",
   339→                params=params,
   340→                headers=_build_headers(),
   341→                timeout=20.0,
   342→            )
   343→            resp.raise_for_status()
   344→            data = resp.json()
   345→    except httpx.ConnectError:
   346→        return to_json({"error": "Could not reach CivitAI API. Check internet connection."})
   347→    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
   348→        return to_json({"error": f"CivitAI API returned {e.response.status_code}."})
   349→    except Exception as e:
   350→        return to_json({"error": f"CivitAI search failed: {e}"})
   351→
   352→    items = data.get("items", [])
   353→    results = [_parse_model(m) for m in items]
   354→
   355→    return to_json({
   356→        "source": "civitai",
   357→        "query": query,
   358→        "type_filter": model_type,
   359→        "base_model_filter": base_model,
   360→        "sort": sort,
   361→        "period": period,
   362→        "results": results,
   363→        "showing": len(results),
   364→        "total_available": data.get("metadata", {}).get("totalItems", len(results)),
   365→    })
   366→
   367→
   368→def _handle_get_civitai_model(tool_input: dict) -> str:
   369→    model_id = tool_input["model_id"]
   370→
   371→    if not CIVITAI_LIMITER().acquire(timeout=5.0):
   372→        return to_json({"error": "Rate limited — too many CivitAI requests. Try again shortly."})
   373→
   374→    try:
   375→        with httpx.Client() as client:
   376→            resp = client.get(
   377→                f"{CIVITAI_API}/models/{model_id}",
   378→                headers=_build_headers(),
   379→                timeout=20.0,
   380→            )
   381→            resp.raise_for_status()
   382→            data = resp.json()
   383→    except httpx.ConnectError:
   384→        return to_json({"error": "Could not reach CivitAI API. Check internet connection."})
   385→    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as e:
   386→        if e.response.status_code == 404:
   387→            return to_json({"error": f"Model {model_id} not found on CivitAI."})
   388→        return to_json({"error": f"CivitAI API returned {e.response.status_code}."})
   389→    except Exception as e:
   390→        return to_json({"error": f"CivitAI request failed: {e}"})
   391→
   392→    return to_json(_parse_model_detail(data))
   393→
   394→
   395→def _handle_get_trending_models(tool_input: dict) -> str:
   396→    model_type = tool_input.get("model_type")
   397→    base_model = tool_input.get("base_model")
   398→    period = tool_input.get("period", "week")
   399→    max_results = min(tool_input.get("max_results", 10), 20)
   400→
   401→    params: dict = {

   403→        "sort": "Most Downloaded",
   404→        "period": _PERIOD_MAP.get(period, "Week"),
   405→        "nsfw": "false",
   406→    }
   407→
   408→    if model_type:
   409→        civitai_type = _TYPE_MAP.get(model_type.lower())

   417→    if not CIVITAI_LIMITER().acquire(timeout=5.0):

1→"""Structured logging with JSON format, rotation, and correlation IDs.
     2→
     3→Provides two formatters:
     4→- JSONFormatter: machine-parseable JSON lines (sort_keys=True for He2025)
     5→- HumanFormatter: clean human-readable output for interactive CLI
     6→
     7→Correlation IDs use thread-local storage to tag all log entries from
     8→a single agent session, making it easy to trace a conversation across
     9→interleaved log output.
    10→"""
    11→
    12→import json
    13→import logging
    14→import logging.handlers
    15→import threading
    16→import uuid
    17→from pathlib import Path
    18→
    19→
    20→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21→# Correlation ID (thread-local)
    22→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    23→
    24→_local = threading.local()
    25→
    26→
    27→def set_correlation_id(corr_id: str | None = None) -> str:
    28→    """Set (or generate) a correlation ID for the current thread.
    29→
    30→    Returns the correlation ID that was set.
    31→    """
    32→    cid = corr_id or uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
    33→    _local.correlation_id = cid
    34→    return cid
    35→
    36→
    37→def get_correlation_id() -> str | None:
    38→    """Get the correlation ID for the current thread, or None."""
    39→    return getattr(_local, "correlation_id", None)
    40→
    41→
    42→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    43→# Formatters
    44→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    45→
    46→class JSONFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    47→    """Emit log records as single-line JSON objects.
    48→
    49→    Fields: timestamp, level, logger, message, correlation_id (if set).
    50→    sort_keys=True for He2025 deterministic serialization.
    51→    """
    52→
    53→    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
    54→        entry = {
    55→            "level": record.levelname,
    56→            "logger": record.name,
    57→            "message": record.getMessage(),
    58→            "timestamp": self.formatTime(record, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
    59→        }
    60→        corr_id = get_correlation_id()
    61→        if corr_id:
    62→            entry["correlation_id"] = corr_id
    63→        if record.exc_info and record.exc_info[1]:
    64→            entry["exception"] = self.formatException(record.exc_info)
    65→        return json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True)
    66→
    67→
    68→class HumanFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    69→    """Clean human-readable log format for interactive CLI use."""
    70→
    71→    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
    72→        corr_id = get_correlation_id()
    73→        prefix = f"[{corr_id}] " if corr_id else ""
    74→        base = f"{prefix}{record.name}: {record.getMessage()}"
    75→        if record.exc_info and record.exc_info[1]:
    76→            base += "\n" + self.formatException(record.exc_info)
    77→        return base
    78→
    79→
    80→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    81→# Setup
    82→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    83→
    84→def setup_logging(
    85→    *,
    86→    level: int = logging.WARNING,
    87→    log_file: Path | str | None = None,
    88→    json_format: bool = False,
    89→    max_bytes: int = 10_000_000,
    90→    backup_count: int = 5,
    91→) -> None:
    92→    """Configure logging for the agent.
    93→
    94→    Args:
    95→        level: Logging level (e.g. logging.DEBUG, logging.WARNING).
    96→        log_file: Optional path to a log file (enables rotation).
    97→        json_format: If True, use JSONFormatter; otherwise HumanFormatter.
    98→        max_bytes: Max log file size before rotation (default 10 MB).
    99→        backup_count: Number of rotated log files to keep.
   100→    """
   101→    root = logging.getLogger()
   102→
   103→    # Remove existing handlers to avoid duplicate output
   104→    root.handlers.clear()
   105→    root.setLevel(level)
   106→
   107→    formatter = JSONFormatter() if json_format else HumanFormatter()
   108→
   109→    # stderr handler (always)
   110→    import sys
   111→    stderr_handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)
   112→    stderr_handler.setFormatter(formatter)
   113→    root.addHandler(stderr_handler)
   114→
   115→    # File handler with rotation (optional)
   116→    if log_file:
   117→        log_path = Path(log_file)
   118→        log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   119→        file_handler = logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler(
   120→            log_path,
   121→            maxBytes=max_bytes,
   122→            backupCount=backup_count,
   123→            encoding="utf-8",
   124→        )
   125→        file_handler.setFormatter(JSONFormatter())  # Always JSON for files
   126→        root.addHandler(file_handler)
   127→

1→"""Model compatibility matrix — prevents mismatched model combos.
     2→
     3→Knowledge base of SD 1.5 / SDXL / Flux / SD3 model families. Cross-references
     4→checkpoint, VAE, ControlNet, and LoRA compatibility based on filename patterns
     5→and base model families. Prevents the "swapped a model and now it crashes" scenario.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→import logging
     9→import re
    10→from pathlib import Path
    11→
    12→from ._util import to_json
    13→
    14→log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    15→
    16→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    17→# Compatibility knowledge base
    18→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    19→
    20→MODEL_FAMILIES = {
    21→    "sd15": {
    22→        "label": "Stable Diffusion 1.5",
    23→        "resolution": "512x512",
    24→        "checkpoint_patterns": [
    25→            r"(?i)sd[-_]?v?1[-_.]?5", r"(?i)sd[-_]?1[-_.]?5",
    26→            r"(?i)realisticVision", r"(?i)dreamshaper",
    27→            r"(?i)deliberate", r"(?i)anything[-_]?v[345]",
    28→            r"(?i)revAnimated", r"(?i)majicmix",
    29→        ],
    30→        "vae_patterns": [
    31→            r"(?i)vae[-_]ft[-_]mse", r"(?i)sd[-_]?v?1.*vae",
    32→            r"(?i)kl[-_]f8[-_]anime",
    33→        ],
    34→        "controlnet_patterns": [
    35→            r"(?i)control_v11p_sd15", r"(?i)control_sd15",
    36→            r"(?i)t2iadapter_.*sd15",
    37→        ],
    38→        "lora_compatible": True,
    39→        "incompatible_families": ["sdxl", "flux", "sd3"],
    40→    },
    41→    "sdxl": {
    42→        "label": "Stable Diffusion XL",
    43→        "resolution": "1024x1024",
    44→        "checkpoint_patterns": [
    45→            r"(?i)sdxl", r"(?i)sd[-_]?xl",
    46→            r"(?i)juggernaut[-_]?xl", r"(?i)dreamshaperXL",
    47→            r"(?i)realvis[-_]?xl", r"(?i)pony",
    48→            r"(?i)colossus", r"(?i)proteus",
    49→        ],
    50→        "vae_patterns": [
    51→            r"(?i)sdxl.*vae", r"(?i)sdxl[-_]vae",
    52→        ],
    53→        "controlnet_patterns": [
    54→            r"(?i)sdxl[-_]controlnet", r"(?i)control.*sdxl",
    55→            r"(?i)diffusers_xl_.*controlnet",
    56→        ],
    57→        "lora_compatible": True,
    58→        "incompatible_families": ["sd15", "flux", "sd3"],
    59→    },
    60→    "flux": {
    61→        "label": "Flux",
    62→        "resolution": "1024x1024",
    63→        "checkpoint_patterns": [
    64→            r"(?i)flux[-_.]?1", r"(?i)flux[-_]dev",
    65→            r"(?i)flux[-_]schnell", r"(?i)flux[-_]fp",
    66→        ],
    67→        "vae_patterns": [
    68→            r"(?i)ae[-_]?t5", r"(?i)flux.*vae",
    69→        ],
    70→        "controlnet_patterns": [
    71→            r"(?i)flux.*controlnet", r"(?i)controlnet.*flux",
    72→            r"(?i)union[-_]pro.*flux",
    73→        ],
    74→        "lora_compatible": True,
    75→        "incompatible_families": ["sd15", "sdxl", "sd3"],
    76→    },
    77→    "sd3": {
    78→        "label": "Stable Diffusion 3",
    79→        "resolution": "1024x1024",
    80→        "checkpoint_patterns": [
    81→            r"(?i)sd[-_]?3", r"(?i)stable[-_]diffusion[-_]?3",
    82→        ],
    83→        "vae_patterns": [
    84→            r"(?i)sd3.*vae",
    85→        ],
    86→        "controlnet_patterns": [
    87→            r"(?i)sd3.*controlnet",
    88→        ],
    89→        "lora_compatible": True,
    90→        "incompatible_families": ["sd15", "sdxl", "flux"],
    91→    },
    92→}
    93→
    94→
    95→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    96→# Tool schemas
    97→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    98→
    99→TOOLS: list[dict] = [
   100→    {
   101→        "name": "check_model_compatibility",
   102→        "description": (
   103→            "Check if models are compatible with each other and the current workflow. "
   104→            "Cross-references checkpoint, VAE, ControlNet, and LoRA by base model "
   105→            "family (SD 1.5 / SDXL / Flux / SD3). Prevents mismatched model combos "
   106→            "that cause silent failures or crashes."
   107→        ),
   108→        "input_schema": {
   109→            "type": "object",
   110→            "properties": {
   111→                "models": {
   112→                    "type": "array",
   113→                    "items": {"type": "string"},
   114→                    "description": (
   115→                        "List of model filenames to check compatibility between. "
   116→                        "Example: ['sdxl_base.safetensors', 'control_v11p_sd15_depth.pth']"
   117→                    ),
   118→                },
   119→                "workflow_path": {
   120→                    "type": "string",
   121→                    "description": (
   122→                        "Optional path to workflow JSON. If provided, extracts model "
   123→                        "references from the workflow and checks compatibility."
   124→                    ),
   125→                },
   126→            },
   127→            "required": [],
   128→        },
   129→    },
   130→    {
   131→        "name": "identify_model_family",
   132→        "description": (
   133→            "Identify which base model family a model file belongs to. "
   134→            "Returns: sd15, sdxl, flux, sd3, or unknown. Use to verify "
   135→            "compatibility before swapping models."
   136→        ),
   137→        "input_schema": {
   138→            "type": "object",
   139→            "properties": {
   140→                "model_name": {
   141→                    "type": "string",
   142→                    "description": "Model filename (e.g., 'realisticVisionV60B1.safetensors').",
   143→                },
   144→            },
   145→            "required": ["model_name"],
   146→        },
   147→    },
   148→]
   149→
   150→
   151→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   152→# Detection logic
   153→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   154→
   155→def _identify_family(model_name: str) -> str:
   156→    """Identify model family from filename using pattern matching."""
   157→    for family_id, family in sorted(MODEL_FAMILIES.items()):
   158→        for pattern_list in [
   159→            family["checkpoint_patterns"],
   160→            family["vae_patterns"],
   161→            family["controlnet_patterns"],
   162→        ]:
   163→            for pattern in pattern_list:
   164→                if re.search(pattern, model_name):
   165→                    return family_id
   166→    return "unknown"
   167→
   168→
   169→def _extract_models_from_workflow(workflow: dict) -> list[str]:
   170→    """Extract model filenames referenced in a workflow."""
   171→    models = []
   172→    model_input_names = {
   173→        "ckpt_name", "vae_name", "lora_name", "control_net_name",
   174→        "model_name", "clip_name", "unet_name",
   175→    }
   176→    for node in workflow.values():
   177→        if not isinstance(node, dict):
   178→            continue
   179→        inputs = node.get("inputs", {})
   180→        for key, value in inputs.items():
   181→            if key in model_input_names and isinstance(value, str):
   182→                models.append(value)
   183→    return sorted(set(models))
   184→
   185→
   186→def _check_compatibility(models: list[str]) -> dict:
   187→    """Check compatibility between a set of models."""
   188→    identified = {}
   189→    for m in models:
   190→        identified[m] = _identify_family(m)
   191→
   192→    # Find unique families (excluding unknown)
   193→    families = set(f for f in identified.values() if f != "unknown")
   194→
   195→    if len(families) <= 1:
   196→        family = families.pop() if families else "unknown"
   197→        return {
   198→            "compatible": True,
   199→            "family": family,
   200→            "family_label": MODEL_FAMILIES.get(family, {}).get("label", "Unknown"),
   201→            "resolution": MODEL_FAMILIES.get(family, {}).get("resolution", "unknown"),
   202→            "models": identified,
   203→            "message": f"All models belong to {MODEL_FAMILIES.get(family, {}).get('label', 'unknown')} family.",
   204→        }
   205→
   206→    # Multiple families detected — incompatible
   207→    conflicts = []
   208→    family_list = sorted(families)
   209→    for i, f1 in enumerate(family_list):
   210→        for f2 in family_list[i + 1:]:
   211→            f1_models = [m for m, f in identified.items() if f == f1]
   212→            f2_models = [m for m, f in identified.items() if f == f2]
   213→            conflicts.append({
   214→                "family_a": f1,
   215→                "family_b": f2,
   216→                "models_a": f1_models,
   217→                "models_b": f2_models,
   218→                "reason": f"{MODEL_FAMILIES[f1]['label']} models are incompatible with {MODEL_FAMILIES[f2]['label']}",
   219→            })
   220→
   221→    return {
   222→        "compatible": False,
   223→        "families_detected": family_list,
   224→        "models": identified,
   225→        "conflicts": conflicts,
   226→        "message": f"Incompatible model families detected: {', '.join(MODEL_FAMILIES[f]['label'] for f in family_list)}",
   227→        "suggestion": f"Use models from the same family. Detected: {', '.join(family_list)}",
   228→    }
   229→
   230→
   231→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   232→# Handlers
   233→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   234→
   235→def _handle_check_compatibility(tool_input: dict) -> str:
   236→    models = tool_input.get("models", [])
   237→    workflow_path = tool_input.get("workflow_path")
   238→
   239→    if workflow_path:
   240→        import json
   241→        path = Path(workflow_path)
   242→        if not path.exists():
   243→            return to_json({"error": f"File not found: {workflow_path}"})
   244→        try:
   245→            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   246→        except Exception as e:
   247→            return to_json({"error": f"Failed to parse workflow: {e}"})
   248→
   249→        # Extract API-format nodes
   250→        if "nodes" in data and isinstance(data["nodes"], list):
   251→            prompt_data = data.get("extra", {}).get("prompt")
   252→            if prompt_data:
   253→                wf_models = _extract_models_from_workflow(prompt_data)
   254→            else:
   255→                wf_models = []
   256→        else:
   257→            wf_models = _extract_models_from_workflow(data)
   258→
   259→        models = sorted(set(models + wf_models))
   260→
   261→    if not models:
   262→        # Try loaded workflow
   263→        from .workflow_patch import get_current_workflow
   264→        wf = get_current_workflow()
   265→        if wf:
   266→            models = _extract_models_from_workflow(wf)
   267→
   268→    if not models:
   269→        return to_json({
   270→            "error": "No models to check. Provide model names, a workflow path, or load a workflow.",
   271→        })
   272→
   273→    result = _check_compatibility(models)
   274→    return to_json(result)

1→"""Circuit breaker pattern for external service calls.
     2→
     3→Prevents cascading failures when ComfyUI or other services are down.
     4→Three states: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (fast-fail), HALF_OPEN (test one request).
     5→
     6→Thread-safe. Used by comfy_api.py to protect against repeated connection failures.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import threading
    11→import time
    12→
    13→log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    14→
    15→# States
    16→CLOSED = "closed"
    17→OPEN = "open"
    18→HALF_OPEN = "half_open"
    19→
    20→
    21→class CircuitBreaker:
    22→    """Thread-safe circuit breaker.
    23→
    24→    Args:
    25→        name: Identifier for logging.
    26→        failure_threshold: Consecutive failures before opening circuit.
    27→        recovery_timeout: Seconds to wait in OPEN state before trying HALF_OPEN.
    28→        half_open_max: Max concurrent requests allowed in HALF_OPEN state.
    29→    """
    30→
    31→    def __init__(
    32→        self,
    33→        name: str = "default",
    34→        failure_threshold: int = 3,
    35→        recovery_timeout: float = 30.0,
    36→        half_open_max: int = 1,
    37→    ):
    38→        self.name = name
    39→        self.failure_threshold = failure_threshold
    40→        self.recovery_timeout = recovery_timeout
    41→        self.half_open_max = half_open_max
    42→
    43→        self._state = CLOSED
    44→        self._failure_count = 0
    45→        self._last_failure_time = 0.0
    46→        self._half_open_count = 0
    47→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
    48→
    49→    @property
    50→    def state(self) -> str:
    51→        with self._lock:
    52→            return self._state
    53→
    54→    def allow_request(self) -> bool:
    55→        """Check if a request should be allowed through.
    56→
    57→        Returns True if request can proceed, False if circuit is open.
    58→        """
    59→        with self._lock:
    60→            if self._state == CLOSED:
    61→                return True
    62→
    63→            if self._state == OPEN:
    64→                elapsed = time.monotonic() - self._last_failure_time
    65→                if elapsed >= self.recovery_timeout:
    66→                    self._state = HALF_OPEN
    67→                    self._half_open_count = 0
    68→                    log.info("Circuit breaker '%s': OPEN -> HALF_OPEN (testing)", self.name)
    69→                    self._half_open_count += 1
    70→                    return True
    71→                return False
    72→
    73→            if self._state == HALF_OPEN:
    74→                if self._half_open_count < self.half_open_max:
    75→                    self._half_open_count += 1
    76→                    return True
    77→                return False
    78→
    79→            return False
    80→
    81→    def record_success(self) -> None:
    82→        """Record a successful request. Resets failure count, closes circuit."""
    83→        with self._lock:
    84→            if self._state != CLOSED:
    85→                log.info("Circuit breaker '%s': %s -> CLOSED (success)", self.name, self._state)
    86→            self._state = CLOSED
    87→            self._failure_count = 0
    88→            self._half_open_count = 0
    89→
    90→    def record_failure(self) -> None:
    91→        """Record a failed request. May open the circuit."""
    92→        with self._lock:
    93→            self._failure_count += 1
    94→            self._last_failure_time = time.monotonic()
    95→
    96→            if self._state == HALF_OPEN:
    97→                self._state = OPEN
    98→                log.warning(
    99→                    "Circuit breaker '%s': HALF_OPEN -> OPEN (test request failed)", self.name
   100→                )
   101→            elif self._failure_count >= self.failure_threshold:
   102→                if self._state != OPEN:
   103→                    log.warning(
   104→                        "Circuit breaker '%s': CLOSED -> OPEN (%d consecutive failures)",
   105→                        self.name,
   106→                        self._failure_count,
   107→                    )
   108→                self._state = OPEN
   109→
   110→    def reset(self) -> None:
   111→        """Reset to initial state. For testing."""
   112→        with self._lock:
   113→            self._state = CLOSED
   114→            self._failure_count = 0
   115→            self._last_failure_time = 0.0
   116→            self._half_open_count = 0
   117→
   118→
   119→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   120→# Global instances
   121→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   122→
   123→_breakers: dict[str, CircuitBreaker] = {}
   124→_registry_lock = threading.Lock()
   125→
   126→
   127→def get_breaker(
   128→    name: str,
   129→    failure_threshold: int = 3,
   130→    recovery_timeout: float = 30.0,
   131→) -> CircuitBreaker:
   132→    """Get or create a named circuit breaker (singleton per name)."""
   133→    with _registry_lock:
   134→        if name not in _breakers:
   135→            _breakers[name] = CircuitBreaker(
   136→                name=name,
   137→                failure_threshold=failure_threshold,
   138→                recovery_timeout=recovery_timeout,
   139→            )
   140→        return _breakers[name]
   141→
   142→
   143→def reset_all() -> None:
   144→    """Reset all circuit breakers. For testing."""
   145→    with _registry_lock:
   146→        _breakers.clear()
   147→
   148→
   149→# Pre-configured breakers
   150→def COMFYUI_BREAKER() -> CircuitBreaker:
   151→    """Circuit breaker for ComfyUI HTTP API calls."""
   152→    return get_breaker("comfyui", failure_threshold=3, recovery_timeout=30.0)
   153→

1→"""Thread-safe token bucket rate limiter with global singleton registry.
     2→
     3→Prevents hammering external APIs (CivitAI, HuggingFace, Claude Vision)
     4→by enforcing configurable rate limits. No external dependencies.
     5→
     6→Usage:
     7→    from .rate_limiter import CIVITAI_LIMITER
     8→    if not CIVITAI_LIMITER().acquire(timeout=5.0):
     9→        return error("Rate limited — try again shortly.")
    10→"""
    11→
    12→import threading
    13→import time
    14→
    15→
    16→class RateLimiter:
    17→    """Token bucket rate limiter — thread-safe, blocking or non-blocking.
    18→
    19→    Args:
    20→        rate: Tokens refilled per second.
    21→        capacity: Maximum burst size (bucket capacity).
    22→    """
    23→
    24→    def __init__(self, rate: float, capacity: int):
    25→        self._rate = rate
    26→        self._capacity = capacity
    27→        self._tokens = float(capacity)
    28→        self._last_refill = time.monotonic()
    29→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
    30→
    31→    def acquire(self, tokens: int = 1, timeout: float | None = None) -> bool:
    32→        """Acquire tokens. Blocks up to `timeout` seconds if needed.
    33→
    34→        Args:
    35→            tokens: Number of tokens to consume (default 1).
    36→            timeout: Max seconds to wait. None = non-blocking (return immediately).
    37→
    38→        Returns:
    39→            True if tokens were acquired, False if timed out or unavailable.
    40→        """
    41→        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout if timeout is not None else None
    42→
    43→        while True:
    44→            with self._lock:
    45→                self._refill()
    46→                if self._tokens >= tokens:
    47→                    self._tokens -= tokens
    48→                    return True
    49→
    50→            # Non-blocking mode — fail immediately
    51→            if deadline is None:
    52→                return False
    53→
    54→            # Check timeout
    55→            now = time.monotonic()
    56→            if now >= deadline:
    57→                return False
    58→
    59→            # Sleep briefly and retry
    60→            wait = min(tokens / self._rate, deadline - now, 0.1)
    61→            time.sleep(wait)
    62→
    63→    def _refill(self) -> None:
    64→        """Refill tokens based on elapsed time. Must be called under lock."""
    65→        now = time.monotonic()
    66→        elapsed = now - self._last_refill
    67→        self._tokens = min(self._capacity, self._tokens + elapsed * self._rate)
    68→        self._last_refill = now
    69→
    70→    @property
    71→    def available(self) -> float:
    72→        """Current token count (approximate — may change between read and use)."""
    73→        with self._lock:
    74→            self._refill()
    75→            return self._tokens
    76→
    77→
    78→class GlobalRateLimiter:
    79→    """Singleton registry of named rate limiters.
    80→
    81→    Ensures only one limiter per resource name exists across the process.
    82→    """
    83→
    84→    _instances: dict[str, RateLimiter] = {}
    85→    _lock = threading.Lock()
    86→
    87→    @classmethod
    88→    def get(cls, resource: str, rate: float, capacity: int) -> RateLimiter:
    89→        """Get or create a rate limiter for the named resource."""
    90→        with cls._lock:
    91→            if resource not in cls._instances:
    92→                cls._instances[resource] = RateLimiter(rate, capacity)
    93→            return cls._instances[resource]
    94→
    95→    @classmethod
    96→    def reset(cls) -> None:
    97→        """Clear all limiters. Use in tests for isolation."""
    98→        with cls._lock:
    99→            cls._instances.clear()
   100→
   101→
   102→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   103→# Pre-configured limiters for each external API
   104→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   105→
   106→def CIVITAI_LIMITER() -> RateLimiter:
   107→    """CivitAI API: 1 req/s sustained, burst of 5."""
   108→    return GlobalRateLimiter.get("civitai", rate=1.0, capacity=5)
   109→
   110→
   111→def HUGGINGFACE_LIMITER() -> RateLimiter:
   112→    """HuggingFace API: 2 req/s sustained, burst of 10."""
   113→    return GlobalRateLimiter.get("huggingface", rate=2.0, capacity=10)
   114→
   115→
   116→def VISION_LIMITER() -> RateLimiter:
   117→    """Claude Vision API: 0.5 req/s sustained, burst of 2."""
   118→    return GlobalRateLimiter.get("vision", rate=0.5, capacity=2)
   119→

     5→_RULES = """\
     6→RULES:
     7→1. NEVER claim to know about specific models from memory. ALWAYS use tools.
     8→2. When asked "what model should I use for X?" — search first, recommend after.
     9→3. When modifying workflows, ALWAYS show the proposed patch and get confirmation before applying.
    10→4. When something fails, read the error, check node compatibility, suggest fixes.
    11→5. Use extended thinking for: workflow design from scratch, debugging, architecture decisions.
    12→6. Use standard responses for: simple queries, status checks, model listings.
    13→7. If ComfyUI is not running, say so immediately. Most tools require it.
    14→8. Prefer /object_info over memory for node interfaces. It's always current.
    15→9. When suggesting new nodes/models, check if they're already installed first.
    16→10. Log key decisions and preferences to session notes (add_note) for continuity.
    17→11. At conversation end, save the session so the user can resume later.
    18→12. Use format='names_only' or format='summary' for large tool queries; drill down with specific tools.
    19→13. For workflow creation, prefer loading a template (list_workflow_templates) and patching it.
    20→14. Before executing, use validate_before_execute to catch errors early.
    21→15. Use add_node/connect_nodes/set_input for building workflows instead of raw JSON patches when possible.
    22→
    23→TOOL OVERVIEW:
    24→
    25→Inspection (live API):
    26→  is_comfyui_running, get_all_nodes, get_node_info, get_system_stats,
    27→  get_queue_status, get_history
    28→
    29→Filesystem:
    30→  list_custom_nodes, list_models, get_models_summary, read_node_source
    31→
    32→Workflow Understanding:
    33→  load_workflow, validate_workflow, get_editable_fields
    34→
    35→Workflow Editing (RFC6902 JSON Patch):
    36→  apply_workflow_patch, preview_workflow_patch, undo_workflow_patch,
    37→  get_workflow_diff, save_workflow, reset_workflow
    38→
    39→Semantic Workflow Building:
    40→  add_node, connect_nodes, set_input
    41→
    42→Execution:

    44→
    45→Discovery:

    52→
    53→Session Memory:

    55→"""
    56→

    60→        "controlnet", "control_net", "depth_map", "canny", "openpose",
    61→        "lineart", "scribble", "ControlNetLoader", "ControlNetApply",

    77→def _detect_relevant_knowledge(session_context: dict | None) -> set[str]:
    78→    """Detect which optional knowledge files to load based on context."""
    79→    triggers = set()

    81→    if not session_context:
    82→        return triggers
    83→
    84→    # Check workflow node types

1→"""Workflow session state container with per-session isolation.
     2→
     3→Provides a dict-like WorkflowSession class that replaces the module-level
     4→_state dict in workflow_patch.py. Enables future multi-session support
     5→via a session registry keyed by session_id.
     6→
     7→Each session holds: loaded_path, base_workflow, current_workflow, history,
     8→and format — the same keys as the original _state dict.
     9→"""
    10→
    11→import copy
    12→import threading
    13→
    14→
    15→class WorkflowSession:
    16→    """Dict-like workflow state container with per-session locking.
    17→
    18→    Implements __getitem__, __setitem__, and .get() so existing code that
    19→    does _state["key"] or _state.get("key") continues to work unchanged.
    20→    """
    21→
    22→    def __init__(self, session_id: str = "default"):
    23→        self.session_id = session_id
    24→        self._data: dict = {
    25→            "loaded_path": None,
    26→            "base_workflow": None,
    27→            "current_workflow": None,
    28→            "history": [],
    29→            "format": None,
    30→        }
    31→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
    32→
    33→    def __getitem__(self, key: str):
    34→        return self._data[key]
    35→
    36→    def __setitem__(self, key: str, value):
    37→        self._data[key] = value
    38→
    39→    def __contains__(self, key: str) -> bool:
    40→        return key in self._data
    41→
    42→    def get(self, key: str, default=None):
    43→        return self._data.get(key, default)
    44→
    45→    def keys(self):
    46→        return self._data.keys()
    47→
    48→    def values(self):
    49→        return self._data.values()
    50→
    51→    def items(self):
    52→        return self._data.items()
    53→
    54→    def update(self, other):
    55→        """Update session data from a dict or another WorkflowSession."""
    56→        if isinstance(other, WorkflowSession):
    57→            self._data.update(other._data)
    58→        else:
    59→            self._data.update(other)
    60→
    61→    def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
    62→        """Support copy.deepcopy() — copies data but creates a fresh lock."""
    63→        new = WorkflowSession(self.session_id)
    64→        new._data = copy.deepcopy(self._data, memo)
    65→        return new
    66→
    67→    def __repr__(self) -> str:
    68→        return f"WorkflowSession(session_id={self.session_id!r}, keys={list(self._data.keys())})"
    69→
    70→
    71→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    72→# Session registry
    73→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    74→
    75→_sessions: dict[str, WorkflowSession] = {}
    76→_registry_lock = threading.Lock()
    77→
    78→
    79→def get_session(session_id: str = "default") -> WorkflowSession:
    80→    """Get or create a workflow session by ID.
    81→
    82→    Thread-safe: concurrent calls with the same session_id return
    83→    the same WorkflowSession instance.
    84→    """
    85→    with _registry_lock:
    86→        if session_id not in _sessions:
    87→            _sessions[session_id] = WorkflowSession(session_id)
    88→        return _sessions[session_id]
    89→
    90→
    91→def clear_sessions() -> None:
    92→    """Remove all sessions from the registry. Used in tests."""
    93→    with _registry_lock:
    94→        _sessions.clear()
    95→

1→"""Session persistence — save and restore agent state across conversations.
     2→
     3→Sessions capture:
     4→- Loaded workflow state (path, base, current, patch history)
     5→- Agent notes (observations, preferences, learnings)
     6→- Metadata (timestamps, tool call counts)
     7→
     8→File format: JSON in sessions/{name}.json with sort_keys=True
     9→for deterministic serialization (He2025 alignment).
    10→"""
    11→
    12→import json
    13→import logging
    14→import shutil
    15→import tempfile
    16→import time
    17→from pathlib import Path
    18→
    19→from ..config import SESSIONS_DIR
    20→
    21→log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    22→
    23→SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
    24→
    25→
    26→def _sessions_dir() -> Path:
    27→    """Ensure sessions directory exists."""
    28→    SESSIONS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    29→    return SESSIONS_DIR
    30→
    31→
    32→def save_session(
    33→    name: str,
    34→    *,
    35→    workflow_state: dict | None = None,
    36→    notes: list[str] | None = None,
    37→    metadata: dict | None = None,
    38→) -> dict:
    39→    """Save session state to a named JSON file.
    40→
    41→    Returns {"saved": path, "size_bytes": n} or {"error": msg}.
    42→    """
    43→    path = _sessions_dir() / f"{name}.json"
    44→
    45→    session_data = {
    46→        "name": name,
    47→        "saved_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
    48→        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
    49→        "workflow": _serialize_workflow_state(workflow_state),
    50→        "notes": notes or [],
    51→        "metadata": metadata or {},
    52→    }
    53→
    54→    try:
    55→        content = json.dumps(session_data, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
    56→        _atomic_write(path, content)
    57→        return {"saved": str(path), "size_bytes": len(content)}
    58→    except Exception as e:
    59→        return {"error": f"Failed to save session: {e}"}
    60→
    61→
    62→def load_session(name: str) -> dict:
    63→    """Load a session from disk.
    64→
    65→    Returns the full session dict or {"error": msg}.
    66→    """
    67→    path = _sessions_dir() / f"{name}.json"
    68→
    69→    if not path.exists():
    70→        # Suggest available sessions
    71→        available = list_sessions()
    72→        names = [s["name"] for s in available.get("sessions", [])]
    73→        if names:
    74→            return {
    75→                "error": f"Session '{name}' not found.",
    76→                "available": names,
    77→            }
    78→        return {"error": f"Session '{name}' not found. No saved sessions exist."}
    79→
    80→    try:
    81→        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    82→        data = _migrate_session(data)
    83→        return data
    84→    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
    85→        return {"error": f"Corrupt session file: {e}"}
    86→    except Exception as e:
    87→        return {"error": f"Failed to load session: {e}"}
    88→
    89→
    90→def list_sessions() -> dict:
    91→    """List all saved sessions with metadata.
    92→
    93→    Returns {"sessions": [...], "count": n, "directory": path}.
    94→    """
    95→    sessions_dir = _sessions_dir()
    96→    sessions = []
    97→
    98→    for path in sorted(sessions_dir.glob("*.json")):
    99→        try:
   100→            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   101→            sessions.append({
   102→                "name": data.get("name", path.stem),
   103→                "saved_at": data.get("saved_at", ""),
   104→                "notes_count": len(data.get("notes", [])),
   105→                "has_workflow": data.get("workflow", {}).get("loaded_path") is not None,
   106→                "file": str(path),
   107→            })
   108→        except Exception:
   109→            sessions.append({
   110→                "name": path.stem,
   111→                "saved_at": "",
   112→                "notes_count": 0,
   113→                "has_workflow": False,
   114→                "file": str(path),
   115→                "error": "corrupt",
   116→            })
   117→
   118→    return {
   119→        "sessions": sessions,
   120→        "count": len(sessions),
   121→        "directory": str(sessions_dir),
   122→    }
   123→
   124→
   125→def add_note(name: str, note: str) -> dict:
   126→    """Add a note to a session (create session if it doesn't exist).
   127→
   128→    Returns {"added": True, "total_notes": n} or {"error": msg}.
   129→    """
   130→    path = _sessions_dir() / f"{name}.json"
   131→
   132→    if path.exists():
   133→        try:
   134→            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   135→        except Exception:
   136→            data = _empty_session(name)
   137→    else:
   138→        data = _empty_session(name)
   139→
   140→    if "notes" not in data:
   141→        data["notes"] = []
   142→
   143→    data["notes"].append({
   144→        "text": note,
   145→        "added_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
   146→    })
   147→    data["saved_at"] = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
   148→
   149→    try:
   150→        content = json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
   151→        _atomic_write(path, content)
   152→        return {"added": True, "total_notes": len(data["notes"])}
   153→    except Exception as e:
   154→        return {"error": f"Failed to save note: {e}"}
   155→
   156→
   157→def restore_workflow_state(session_data: dict) -> dict | None:
   158→    """Extract workflow state from session data for re-loading.
   159→
   160→    Returns the workflow state dict, or None if no workflow was saved.
   161→    """
   162→    wf = session_data.get("workflow")
   163→    if not wf or not wf.get("loaded_path"):
   164→        return None
   165→    return wf
   166→
   167→
   168→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   169→# Internal helpers
   170→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   171→
   172→def _migrate_session(data: dict) -> dict:
   173→    """Upgrade session data from older schema versions to current.
   174→
   175→    v0 -> v1: adds schema_version field.
   176→    """
   177→    version = data.get("schema_version", 0)
   178→    if version < 1:
   179→        data["schema_version"] = 1
   180→        log.debug("Migrated session '%s' from v0 to v1", data.get("name", "?"))
   181→    return data
   182→
   183→
   184→def _atomic_write(path: Path, content: str) -> None:
   185→    """Write content to path atomically using temp-file-then-rename.
   186→
   187→    Prevents corrupt session files from interrupted writes.
   188→    """
   189→    fd = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
   190→        mode="w",
   191→        encoding="utf-8",
   192→        dir=path.parent,
   193→        suffix=".tmp",
   194→        delete=False,
   195→    )
   196→    try:
   197→        fd.write(content)
   198→        fd.close()
   199→        shutil.move(fd.name, str(path))
   200→    except Exception:
   201→        # Clean up temp file on failure
   202→        try:
   203→            Path(fd.name).unlink(missing_ok=True)
   204→        except Exception:
   205→            pass
   206→        raise
   207→
   208→
   209→def _empty_session(name: str) -> dict:
   210→    return {
   211→        "name": name,
   212→        "saved_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
   213→        "workflow": {"loaded_path": None, "format": None},
   214→        "notes": [],
   215→        "metadata": {},
   216→    }
   217→
   218→
   219→def _serialize_workflow_state(state: dict | None) -> dict:
   220→    """Serialize workflow_patch._state for disk storage."""
   221→    if state is None:
   222→        return {"loaded_path": None, "format": None}
   223→
   224→    return {
   225→        "loaded_path": state.get("loaded_path"),
   226→        "format": state.get("format"),
   227→        "base_workflow": state.get("base_workflow"),
   228→        "current_workflow": state.get("current_workflow"),
   229→        "history_depth": len(state.get("history", [])),
   230→        # Don't serialize full history — can be large.
   231→        # User can undo from current_workflow vs base.
   232→    }
   233→

1→"""Agent loop — the core of the ComfyUI Agent.
     2→
     3→Uses the Anthropic API with streaming tool-use to run an interactive agent.
     4→The agent decides which tools to call; we execute them and feed results back.
     5→
     6→Includes streaming responses, context management, retry logic, and logging.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import concurrent.futures
    10→import logging
    11→import threading
    12→import time
    13→
    14→import anthropic
    15→
    16→from .config import (
    17→    AGENT_MODEL, MAX_TOKENS, MAX_AGENT_TURNS,
    18→    COMPACT_THRESHOLD, API_MAX_RETRIES, API_RETRY_DELAY,
    19→)
    20→from .logging_config import set_correlation_id
    21→from .system_prompt import build_system_prompt
    22→from .tools import ALL_TOOLS, handle as handle_tool
    23→
    24→log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    25→
    26→# Graceful shutdown flag — checked at top of each agent turn
    27→_shutdown = threading.Event()
    28→
    29→
    30→def request_shutdown() -> None:
    31→    """Signal the agent loop to exit gracefully."""
    32→    _shutdown.set()
    33→
    34→
    35→def create_client() -> anthropic.Anthropic:
    36→    """Create Anthropic client (reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from env)."""
    37→    return anthropic.Anthropic()
    38→
    39→
    40→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    41→# Context management
    42→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    43→
    44→def _estimate_tokens(messages: list[dict]) -> int:
    45→    """Rough token estimate (~4 chars per token)."""
    46→    total = 0
    47→    for msg in messages:
    48→        content = msg.get("content", "")
    49→        if isinstance(content, str):
    50→            total += len(content) // 4
    51→        elif isinstance(content, list):
    52→            for item in content:
    53→                if isinstance(item, dict):
    54→                    total += len(str(item.get("content", ""))) // 4
    55→                elif hasattr(item, "text"):
    56→                    total += len(item.text) // 4
    57→                elif hasattr(item, "input"):
    58→                    total += len(str(item.input)) // 4
    59→                else:
    60→                    total += len(str(item)) // 4
    61→    return total
    62→
    63→
    64→def _summarize_dropped(messages: list[dict]) -> str:
    65→    """Build a structured summary of dropped messages for context continuity.
    66→
    67→    Extracts: user requests, tool calls made, key decisions/results, and workflow state.
    68→    """
    69→    sections = {
    70→        "user_requests": [],
    71→        "tools_called": [],
    72→        "key_results": [],
    73→        "workflow_info": None,
    74→    }
    75→
    76→    for msg in messages:
    77→        role = msg.get("role", "")
    78→        content = msg.get("content", "")
    79→
    80→        if role == "user" and isinstance(content, str):
    81→            # Capture user requests (first 100 chars each)
    82→            text = content.strip()
    83→            if text and not text.startswith("["):  # Skip system summaries
    84→                sections["user_requests"].append(text[:100])
    85→
    86→        elif role == "user" and isinstance(content, list):
    87→            # Extract tool results summary
    88→            for block in content:
    89→                if not isinstance(block, dict) or block.get("type") != "tool_result":
    90→                    continue
    91→                result_text = block.get("content", "")
    92→                if not isinstance(result_text, str):
    93→                    continue
    94→                # Extract key info from tool results
    95→                if '"loaded_path"' in result_text or '"saved"' in result_text:
    96→                    try:
    97→                        import json
    98→                        data = json.loads(result_text)
    99→                        path = data.get("loaded_path") or data.get("saved") or data.get("file")
   100→                        if path:
   101→                            sections["workflow_info"] = path
   102→                    except Exception:
   103→                        pass
   104→
   105→        elif role == "assistant" and isinstance(content, list):
   106→            # Extract tool call names from assistant content blocks
   107→            for block in content:
   108→                if hasattr(block, "type") and block.type == "tool_use":
   109→                    sections["tools_called"].append(block.name)
   110→                elif isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_use":
   111→                    sections["tools_called"].append(block.get("name", "?"))
   112→
   113→    # Build structured summary
   114→    lines = ["[Context Summary - earlier messages compacted]"]
   115→
   116→    if sections["user_requests"]:
   117→        lines.append("Topics discussed: " + "; ".join(sections["user_requests"][:5]))
   118→
   119→    if sections["tools_called"]:
   120→        # Deduplicate, preserve order
   121→        seen = set()
   122→        unique = []
   123→        for t in sections["tools_called"]:
   124→            if t not in seen:

   127→        lines.append("Tools used: " + ", ".join(unique))
   128→
   129→    if sections["workflow_info"]:
   130→        lines.append(f"Workflow context: {sections['workflow_info']}")
   131→
   132→    lines.append("Recent conversation follows.")
   133→    return "\n".join(lines)
   134→
   135→
   136→def _compact_messages(messages: list[dict], threshold: int) -> list[dict]:
   137→    """Compact messages to stay within context budget.
   138→
   139→    Strategy:
   140→      1. Mask old tool results (replace processed results with compact references)
   141→      2. Truncate remaining large tool results > 2000 chars
   142→      3. If still over, drop oldest exchanges with structured summary
   143→    """
   144→    estimated = _estimate_tokens(messages)
   145→    if estimated <= threshold:
   146→        return messages
   147→
   148→    log.info("Context at ~%d tokens, compacting (threshold: %d)", estimated, threshold)
   149→
   150→    # Pass 1: Truncate large tool results
   151→    compacted = []
   152→    for msg in messages:
   153→        if msg["role"] == "user" and isinstance(msg.get("content"), list):
   154→            new_content = []
   155→            for block in msg["content"]:
   156→                if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_result":
   157→                    content = block.get("content", "")
   158→                    if isinstance(content, str) and len(content) > 2000:
   159→                        block = {**block, "content": content[:2000] + "\n[...truncated]"}
   160→                new_content.append(block)
   161→            compacted.append({**msg, "content": new_content})
   162→        else:
   163→            compacted.append(msg)
   164→
   165→    estimated = _estimate_tokens(compacted)
   166→    if estimated <= threshold:
   167→        log.info("Compacted to ~%d tokens via tool result truncation", estimated)
   168→        return compacted
   169→
   170→    # Pass 2: Drop oldest exchanges with structured summary
   171→    keep_recent = 6
   172→    if len(compacted) > keep_recent:
   173→        dropped = compacted[:-keep_recent]
   174→        dropped_count = len(dropped)
   175→        summary_text = _summarize_dropped(dropped)
   176→        summary_msg = {"role": "user", "content": summary_text}
   177→        compacted = [summary_msg] + compacted[-keep_recent:]
   178→        log.info("Dropped %d older messages, keeping %d recent", dropped_count, keep_recent)
   179→
   180→    return compacted
   181→
   182→
   183→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   184→# Observation masking
   185→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   186→
   187→_MASK_THRESHOLD = 1500  # chars — tool results larger than this get masked after processing
   188→
   189→
   190→def _mask_processed_results(messages: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
   191→    """Replace large tool results in older turns with compact summaries.
   192→
   193→    Only masks results from turns that have already been processed
   194→    (i.e., there's a subsequent assistant message). The most recent
   195→    tool results are kept intact since the model hasn't responded to them yet.
   196→    """
   197→    if len(messages) < 3:
   198→        return messages
   199→
   200→    # Find the last user message with tool_results (the one the model hasn't processed yet)
   201→    last_tool_result_idx = -1
   202→    for i in range(len(messages) - 1, -1, -1):
   203→        msg = messages[i]
   204→        if msg["role"] == "user" and isinstance(msg.get("content"), list):
   205→            has_tool_result = any(
   206→                isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_result"
   207→                for b in msg["content"]
   208→            )
   209→            if has_tool_result:
   210→                last_tool_result_idx = i
   211→                break
   212→
   213→    masked = []
   214→    for i, msg in enumerate(messages):
   215→        # Only mask tool results that are NOT the most recent batch
   216→        if (
   217→            i < last_tool_result_idx
   218→            and msg["role"] == "user"
   219→            and isinstance(msg.get("content"), list)
   220→        ):
   221→            new_content = []
   222→            for block in msg["content"]:
   223→                if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "tool_result":
   224→                    content = block.get("content", "")
   225→                    if isinstance(content, str) and len(content) > _MASK_THRESHOLD:
   226→                        # Build compact reference
   227→                        preview = content[:200]
   228→                        char_count = len(content)
   229→                        block = {
   230→                            **block,
   231→                            "content": (
   232→                                f"[Processed result ({char_count} chars)]\n"
   233→                                f"{preview}...\n"
   234→                                f"[Full output was processed in prior turn]"
   235→                            ),
   236→                        }
   237→                new_content.append(block)
   238→            masked.append({**msg, "content": new_content})
   239→        else:

   242→    return masked

   249→def _stream_with_retry(
   250→    client,
   251→    *,
   252→    model,
   253→    max_tokens,
   254→    system,
   255→    tools,
   256→    messages,
   257→    on_text_delta=None,
   258→    on_thinking_delta=None,

   261→
   262→    Returns the final Message object.
   263→    """
   264→    last_error = None
   265→
   266→    for attempt in range(API_MAX_RETRIES + 1):
   267→        try:
   268→            with client.messages.stream(
   269→                model=model,
   270→                max_tokens=max_tokens,
   271→                system=system,
   272→                tools=tools,
   273→                messages=messages,
   274→            ) as stream:
   275→                for event in stream:
   276→                    if event.type == "content_block_delta":
   277→                        delta = event.delta
   278→                        if hasattr(delta, "text") and on_text_delta:

   287→                delay = API_RETRY_DELAY * (2 ** attempt)
   288→                log.warning("Rate limited, retrying in %.1fs (attempt %d)", delay, attempt + 1)
   289→                time.sleep(delay)
   290→            else:
   291→                raise
   292→
   293→        except anthropic.APIConnectionError as e:
   294→            last_error = e
   295→            if attempt < API_MAX_RETRIES:
   296→                delay = API_RETRY_DELAY * (2 ** attempt)
   297→                log.warning("Connection error, retrying in %.1fs: %s", delay, e)
   298→                time.sleep(delay)
   299→            else:
   300→                raise
   301→
   302→        except anthropic.APIStatusError as e:
   303→            last_error = e
   304→            if e.status_code >= 500 and attempt < API_MAX_RETRIES:
   305→                delay = API_RETRY_DELAY * (2 ** attempt)
   306→                log.warning("Server error %d, retrying in %.1fs", e.status_code, delay)
   307→                time.sleep(delay)
   308→            else:
   309→                raise
   310→
   311→    raise last_error  # pragma: no cover
   312→
   313→
   314→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   315→# Agent turn
   316→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   317→
   318→def run_agent_turn(
   319→    client: anthropic.Anthropic,
   320→    messages: list[dict],
   321→    system: str,
   322→    *,
   323→    on_text_delta: callable = None,
   324→    on_tool_call: callable = None,
   325→    on_thinking_delta: callable = None,
   326→    on_stream_end: callable = None,
   327→) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:
   328→    """
   329→    Run one agent turn with streaming.
   330→
   331→    Returns (updated_messages, done) where done=True means the agent
   332→    produced a final text response with no tool calls.
   333→    """
   334→    # Check for graceful shutdown request
   335→    if _shutdown.is_set():
   336→        log.info("Shutdown requested — exiting agent turn")
   337→        return messages, True
   338→
   339→    # Mask processed tool results, then compact if still over budget
   340→    messages = _mask_processed_results(messages)
   341→    messages = _compact_messages(messages, COMPACT_THRESHOLD)
   342→
   343→    t0 = time.monotonic()
   344→
   345→    response = _stream_with_retry(
   346→        client,
   347→        model=AGENT_MODEL,
   348→        max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS,
   349→        system=system,
   350→        tools=ALL_TOOLS,
   351→        messages=messages,
   352→        on_text_delta=on_text_delta,
   353→        on_thinking_delta=on_thinking_delta,
   354→    )
   355→
   356→    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
   357→    log.debug("API response in %.1fs, stop_reason=%s", elapsed, response.stop_reason)
   358→
   359→    # Signal stream end (for newline handling in CLI)
   360→    if on_stream_end:
   361→        on_stream_end()
   362→
   363→    # Process tool calls from the complete response
   364→    assistant_content = response.content
   365→    has_tool_use = False
   366→    tool_results = []
   367→
   368→    # Collect tool calls
   369→    tool_calls = [block for block in assistant_content if block.type == "tool_use"]
   370→    has_tool_use = len(tool_calls) > 0
   371→
   372→    if len(tool_calls) > 1:
   373→        # Execute multiple tool calls in parallel
   374→        for tc in tool_calls:
   375→            if on_tool_call:
   376→                on_tool_call(tc.name, tc.input)
   377→
   378→        def _run_tool(tc):
   379→            t_tool = time.monotonic()
   380→            result = handle_tool(tc.name, tc.input)
   381→            log.debug("Tool %s completed in %.2fs", tc.name, time.monotonic() - t_tool)
   382→            return tc.id, result
   383→
   384→        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
   385→            futures = {executor.submit(_run_tool, tc): tc for tc in tool_calls}
   386→            results_map = {}
   387→            for future in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures):
   388→                tool_id, result = future.result()
   389→                results_map[tool_id] = result
   390→
   391→        # Preserve original order
   392→        for tc in tool_calls:
   393→            tool_results.append({
   394→                "type": "tool_result",
   395→                "tool_use_id": tc.id,
   396→                "content": results_map[tc.id],
   397→            })
   398→    elif len(tool_calls) == 1:
   399→        # Single tool call — run directly (no thread overhead)
   400→        tc = tool_calls[0]
   401→        if on_tool_call:
   402→            on_tool_call(tc.name, tc.input)
   403→        t_tool = time.monotonic()
   404→        result = handle_tool(tc.name, tc.input)
   405→        log.debug("Tool %s completed in %.2fs", tc.name, time.monotonic() - t_tool)
   406→        tool_results.append({
   407→            "type": "tool_result",
   408→            "tool_use_id": tc.id,
   409→            "content": result,
   410→        })
   411→
   412→    # Append assistant message
   413→    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": assistant_content})
   414→
   415→    if has_tool_use:
   416→        # Feed tool results back
   417→        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": tool_results})
   418→        return messages, False
   419→    else:
   420→        # No tool calls — agent is done with this turn
   421→        return messages, True
   422→
   423→
   424→def run_interactive(
   425→    client: anthropic.Anthropic,
   426→    *,
   427→    session_context: dict | None = None,
   428→    on_text_delta: callable = None,
   429→    on_tool_call: callable = None,
   430→    on_thinking_delta: callable = None,
   431→    on_stream_end: callable = None,
   432→    on_user_input: callable = None,
   433→) -> None:
   434→    """
   435→    Run the full interactive agent loop with streaming.
   436→
   437→    Args:
   438→        session_context: Optional session data for context-aware system prompt.
   439→
   440→    Callbacks:
   441→        on_text_delta(text)      — incremental text chunk (streaming)
   442→        on_tool_call(name, inp)  — agent is calling a tool
   443→        on_thinking_delta(text)  — thinking text chunk (streaming)
   444→        on_stream_end()          — stream finished (for newline handling)
   445→        on_user_input()          — should return user input string, or None to quit
   446→    """
   447→    set_correlation_id()  # Unique ID for this session's log entries
   448→    system = build_system_prompt(session_context=session_context)
   449→    messages = []
   450→
   451→    while True:
   452→        # Get user input
   453→        if on_user_input:
   454→            user_text = on_user_input()
   455→        else:
   456→            user_text = input("> ")
   457→
   458→        if user_text is None:
   459→            break
   460→
   461→        user_text = user_text.strip()
   462→        if not user_text:
   463→            continue
   464→
   465→        if user_text.lower() in ("quit", "exit", "q"):
   466→            break
   467→
   468→        # Add user message
   469→        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_text})
   470→
   471→        # Run agent turns until it produces a final response
   472→        turns = 0
   473→        while turns < MAX_AGENT_TURNS:
   474→            turns += 1
   475→            try:
   476→                messages, done = run_agent_turn(
   477→                    client,
   478→                    messages,
   479→                    system,
   480→                    on_text_delta=on_text_delta,
   481→                    on_tool_call=on_tool_call,
   482→                    on_thinking_delta=on_thinking_delta,
   483→                    on_stream_end=on_stream_end,
   484→                )
   485→            except anthropic.APIError as e:
   486→                log.error("API error after retries: %s", e)
   487→                if on_text_delta:
   488→                    on_text_delta(f"\n[API error: {e}. Try again.]\n")
   489→                if on_stream_end:
   490→                    on_stream_end()
   491→                break
   492→
   493→            if done:
   494→                break
   495→
   496→        if turns >= MAX_AGENT_TURNS:
   497→            if on_text_delta:
   498→                on_text_delta(
   499→                    f"\n[Agent hit max turns ({MAX_AGENT_TURNS}). Ready for next input.]\n"
   500→                )
   501→            if on_stream_end:
   502→                on_stream_end()
   503→
